messages:
maria_support: heads up @olga_engineer @devon_infra — customer ticket #C-9442: batch rerank call returned aligned-but-shifted candidates and some very odd scores. they saw unexpected negatives and a few 500s. link: https://support.example.com/C-9442 :wave:

olga_engineer: on it. can you paste a minimal repro payload? sounds like per-query candidate list alignment issues (candidates moved between queries) rather than ranker model weights changing.

maria_support: pasting redacted sample below (they say we ingest via gzip streaming):

maria_support: ```json
[
  {"query_id":"q1","query":"how to reset password","candidates":["c1","c2","c3"]},
  {"query_id":"q2","query":"change email","candidates":["c4","c5"]},
  {"query_id":"q3","query":"2fa not working","candidates":["c6","c7","c8","c9"]}
]
```

maria_support: they call /v1/rerank/batch with a top-level array. when we respond, scores for q2 looked like they referenced c2/c3 from q1.

rerank-bot: ERROR [2145012346] request_id=rr-9f2a: candidate-index-out-of-range at scorer.py:412 -> "per-query candidate alignment mismatch"

devon_infra: can you also paste the raw bytes/headers? if they're streaming gzipped JSONL there's a known edge case where chunk boundary splits an array token and the parser concatenates incorrectly. any chance the client is sending `Content-Encoding: gzip` plus chunked chunking?

maria_support: customer says they used our python SDK with streaming enabled. headers: `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. attaching small excerpt of the server side parse log: ```
2026-02-18T14:12:03Z parse: begin_stream
2026-02-18T14:12:03Z parse: buffer flush (chunk size=8192)
2026-02-18T14:12:03Z parse: JSON array open, expecting objects
2026-02-18T14:12:04Z parse: partial object concatenated across chunks
2026-02-18T14:12:04Z scorer: mapped candidate indices -> global offset +5
```

olga_engineer: that log is telling. likely the streaming decompressor yields partial tokens and our array-flattening path reconstructs items but loses per-query separators. i can reproduce locally with a hacked client that gzips then emits chunks mid-object.

devon_infra: please add a failing unit test to the ingest parser. quick repro script (run locally):

devon_infra: ```bash
python - <<'PY'
import gzip, socket, time, json
payload = json.dumps([{"query":"a","candidates":["x","y"]},{"query":"b","candidates":["z"]}])
compressed = gzip.compress(payload.encode())
# send compressed in two halves to mimic chunked stream
first = compressed[:len(compressed)//2]
second = compressed[len(compressed)//2:]
# feed into our parser binary or curl with --data-binary @-
print('first len', len(first), 'second len', len(second))
PY
```

olga_engineer: thanks. i'll push a parser patch to validate that for each query object we read a candidates array and the sum of lengths matches expected. fail fast with 400 + diagnostic to help callers.

maria_support: customer impact: they reported 3 requests failed with 500s and around 14 requests returned misaligned scores. they flagged that billing looked off (token counts spiked). @billing_bot any auto-detection?

billing_bot: noticed anomalous token usage for acct_1138 between 2026-02-18T14:10 and 14:15. flagged for review. suggested adjustment: issue provisional credit if root cause confirmed.

tuan_pm: what's ETA to patch? customer asks for repro steps to validate before we refund. also need to know whether tokens were double-counted or if some requests got reprocessed.

olga_engineer: patch is small. enforce strict parser boundaries + add metric emit when alignment mismatch detected. aim to open PR in 2h. canary rollout same day if tests pass.

sre_oncall: we saw a latency blip coincident with the timeframe: p95 went from 120ms to 450ms for rerank batch endpoint. correlating with higher CPU on the ingest workers. i'll coordinate canary and watch error budget.

devon_infra: quick mitigation: return 400 with `error: per_query_candidates_mismatch` when we detect inconsistent counts, rather than silently mapping. that'll reduce misbilling by dropping malformed requests immediately.

maria_support: i'll reply to the customer with repro steps and temporary mitigation. sample message: "We've identified a parsing edge-case for gzipped chunked requests that can lead to candidate alignment issues. Please avoid streaming gzipped arrays; send a single gzipped payload or use non-chunked upload while we patch. We will follow up with a fix and potential credit."

tuan_pm: please include ETA and whether this impacts historical billing.

billing_bot: flagged all transactions from acct_1138 for manual review. will hold auto-invoicing for 48h.

olga_engineer: PR: open -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingest/merge/2231. changes: strict JSON streaming parser, validation hook, clearer 400 body. i'll add unit test that reproduces chunk-split case.

devon_infra: i'll schedule a canary at 15:30 UTC with 5% traffic and observe alignment_error metric. rollback if >1% errors or p95 > 250ms.

maria_support: thanks all. i'll send customer update and mark ticket. ping me when canary is green so i can close the loop. :thumbsup:

olga_engineer: will also add a short note to SDK docs warning about Content-Encoding + Transfer-Encoding combinations until servers accept them safely.

maria_support: noted. closing actions: olga -> PR and tests; devon -> canary; billing_bot -> provisional hold; maria -> customer update.

sre_oncall: acknowledged. monitoring alert set: `rerank.alignment_error_rate > 0.2%` -> pager.

maria_support: cheers, updating ticket now :white_check_mark:
